main_text.p: humanitate superaverit, placaverit submissiohe: verf. 10.{h}Sic (inquit) vidi faciem tuam, quasi viderim vultum Dei: & paulo post, 15.{i}hoc unum tantum indigeo, ut inveniam gratiam in conspectu tuo Domine mi.

Capite{k} sequente, legimus Simeonem & Levi ob raptum sororis suae Dinae, Principes terrae illius Sichem & Hemor Idololatras quidem, sed tamen legitimos, per dolum malum interfecis-se, sed quo eventu? certe non alio quam ut & incolarum istius loci odium, & sui patris{l} maledictionem incurrerent. Ita enim silicernius senex, & jamjam moribundus, cum aliis filiis benediceret eorum capita devovet:{m} Simeon & Levi, fratres, vasa iniquitatis, bellantia, in consilium eorum non veniat anima mea, & in coetu eorum non sit gloria mea; quia in furore suo occiderunt virum, & in voluntate sua suffoderunt murum; maledictus furor eorum quia pertinax, & indignatio illorum quia dura; dividam eos in Jacob, & dispergam eos in Israel.

page.notes: <note letter="k" side="right">Cap. 34.</note> <note letter="l" side="right">verf. 29.</note> <note letter="m" side="right">Ge. 49. 5.</note> Doubtful: the note marked "i" reads "15" with an uncertain mark after it. "submissiohe" is printed as "fubmiffiohe" and may be a printing error. "silicernius" is printed with a long s that looks like f. Notes k, l and m are placed at their text marks and also listed in the footnote paragraphs. The left edge shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.
